title: Weathering With You
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Manga adaptation of Makoto Shinkai's film. High-school freshman Hodaka runs away from his island home to Tokyo, where he meets Hina, a girl whose power can change the weather, and the story explores love and sacrifice as he tries to protect her (Kodansha blurb via AniList/MU; Common Sense Media guide to the film).
life_message: Love for one person can be worth defying the world's expectations, though choices about nature carry real costs.

content.note: In the film Hodaka is beaten in street fights and by police and fires a gun twice without hitting anyone (CSM); AniList Guns, Police.
Dangerous storms; peril to the leads (CSM, film).
Teen first love, hand-holding; in the film men pressure a young woman toward a 'sex club' job (CSM). Manga handling to verify.
Mild profanity in the film (CSM); manga to verify.
Adults drink and smoke; a 16-year-old is offered beer (CSM, film).
Loneliness of a runaway; Hina's personal cost (CSM).

Film tie-in; real brands appear in the film (CSM).

folkways.japan: The weather maiden draws on Japanese shrine and kami traditions, and the urban poverty of youths reflects modern Tokyo, described as context.

delivery.evidence: CSM (film): 'an underlying but not heavy-handed environmentalist message'.
delivery.note: Adults such as Natsumi and Suga help Hodaka while police and other adults oppose him (CSM).

winners_losers: Sympathy rests with Hodaka and Hina; adult institutions that would separate them are cast as obstacles.
